ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r1.claim: The answer to “whoever allies himself” may be omitted and inferred as “he joins God’s party and prevails.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r1.anchor: لدلالة ما بعده عليه، أي: يكن من حزب الله ويغلب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r2.claim: Alternatively, the following clause is the answer, with an explicit noun replacing the pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الجواب: فإن حزب الله، ويكون من وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r3.claim: Naming God's party explicitly honors and distinguishes its members through their association with God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r3.anchor: وفائدة وضع الظاهر هنا موضع المضمر الإضافة إلى الله تعالى فيشرفون بذلك، وصاروا بذلك أعلاما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r4.claim: A hizb is a group gathered together for a common purpose.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r4.anchor: وأصل الحزب القوم يجتمعون لأمر حزبهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r5.claim: Zamakhshari reads the party as God, the Messenger, and the believers collectively; Abū Ḥayyān considers this parsing syntactically strained.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد حزب الله والرسول والمؤمنين، ويكون المعنى: ومن يتولهم فقد تولى حزب الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya explains that whoever allies with God and His messenger prevails over every opponent because he belongs to God's victorious party.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطية: أي فإنه غالب كل من ناوأه، وجاءت العبارة عامة إن حزب الله هم الغالبون اختصارا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r7.claim: The relative pronoun 'whoever' is generic rather than singular, and 'they' may be a separator or the subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p301/r7.anchor: ومن يراد بها الجنس لا مفرد، وهم هنا يحتمل أن يكون فصلا، ويحتمل أن يكون مبتدأ

NAHHAS:v2p28/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p28/r1.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v2p28/r1.claim: One analysis supplies an omitted predicate: whoever allies with God, His Messenger, and believers is in God's party.
NAHHAS:v2p28/r1.anchor: فقيل الخبر محذوف والتقدير ومن يتول الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا فهو من حزب الله

NAHHAS:v2p28/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p28/r2.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v2p28/r2.claim: Another analysis makes هم the predicate and الغالبون a second predicate.
NAHHAS:v2p28/r2.anchor: وقيل ( هم ) الخبر و ( الغالبون ) خبر ثان

STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r31.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r31.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r31.claim: Verses 5:51–57 set political boundaries by warning Muslims against taking Jews and Christians as protectors to the exclusion of their own religious community.
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r31.anchor: in vv. 51–57, political boundaries are established between these communities, as Muslims are warned not to take Jews and Christians as protectors to the exclusion of members of the Muslim religious community

STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r32.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r32.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r32.claim: Islamic Law allows treaties of alliance between Muslim states and Christian or Jewish political entities.
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r32.anchor: Islamic Law does allow treaties of alliance between the Muslim state, or states, and Christian or Jewish political entities).

THALABI:v4p81/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p81/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
THALABI:v4p81/r4.claim: He interprets the believers as protectors of one another and says whoever takes God, the Messenger, and the believers as allies belongs to God's victorious party.
THALABI:v4p81/r4.anchor: قال: سألت أبا جعفر عن قوله إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا قال: هم المؤمنون بعضهم أولياء بعض

THALABI:v4p81/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p81/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p81/r5.claim: The word ḥizb means supporter, as illustrated by the rajaz line about Bilal being in the speaker's party.
THALABI:v4p81/r5.anchor: قال الراجز: وكيف أضوي وبلال حزبي أي ناصري

THALABI:v4p81/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p81/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p81/r6.claim: God's party are the victorious ones.
THALABI:v4p81/r6.anchor: هم الغالبون يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الذين اتخذوا دينكم هزوا ولعبا الآية

STUDYQURAN:5:56/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:56/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:56/r1.claim: Those following 5:51 and 5:55 by taking God, the Messengers, and believers as protectors are called God's party; the term has been adopted by Islamic groups, including Hezbollah in Lebanon.
STUDYQURAN:5:56/r1.anchor: Those who follow the injunction in vv. 51 and 55 to avoid taking protectors other than God, the Messengers, and the believers, are here described as the party of God

STUDYQURAN:5:56/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:56/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:56/r2.claim: God's party in 58:22 consists of those who prosper and are content with God and whom God is pleased with; it is contrasted with Satan's party in 58:19.
STUDYQURAN:5:56/r2.anchor: Party of God is also used in 58:22, where it is described as consisting of those who shall prosper

TAB-FULL:v8p529/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r3.speaker: عبادة بن الوليد بن عبادة بن الصامت
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r3.claim: The verse was reportedly revealed when ʿUbādah renounced his alliance with Banū Qaynuqāʿ after their war with Muhammad and declared allegiance to God, the Messenger, and the believers.
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r3.anchor: عن عبادة بن الوليد بن عبادة بن الصامت، قال: لما حاربت بنو قينقاع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، مشى عبادة بن الصامت إلى رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v8p532/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p532/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p532/r1.claim: God assures those who disavowed Jewish alliances, and those tempted to retain them out of fear, that whoever trusts and allies with God, His Messenger, and the believers will prevail over opponents as God’s party.
TAB-FULL:v8p532/r1.anchor: وهذا إعلام من الله تعالى ذكره عباده جميعا , الذين تبرءوا من اليهود وحلفهم

TAB-FULL:v8p532/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p532/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p532/r2.claim: God’s allies win and rule against their enemies because they are God’s party, which prevails over Satan’s party.
TAB-FULL:v8p532/r2.anchor: لهم الغلبة والدوائر والدولة على من عاداهم وحادهم، لأنهم حزب الله، وحزب الله هم الغالبون دون حزب الشيطان

TAB-FULL:v8p532/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p532/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p532/r3.claim: Ḥizb means supporters; the verse’s party of God are God’s helpers.
TAB-FULL:v8p532/r3.anchor: ويعني بقوله: {فإن حزب الله} [المائدة: 56] فإن أنصار الله

TAB-FULL:v8p532/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p532/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v8p532/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says God tells the believers not to fear losing political power or a calamity; the party consists of supporters.
TAB-FULL:v8p532/r4.anchor: عن السدي، قال: أخبرهم يعني الرب، تعالى ذكره من الغالب، فقال: لا تخافوا الدولة ولا الدائرة

TAB-FULL:v8p532/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p532/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p532/r5.claim: A rajaz line uses aḍwā for being weakened or oppressed and “my party” (ḥizbī) for my supporter.
TAB-FULL:v8p532/r5.anchor: يعني بقوله أضوى: أستضعف وأضام، من الشيء الضاوي. ويعني بقوله: وبلال حزبي، يعني ناصري

TABATABAI:5:55-56/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56/r1.speaker: جماعة من مفسري القوم
TABATABAI:5:55-56/r1.claim: Some exegetes treat these verses as continuous with the bans on alliance and read wilaya as support, restricted to God, the Messenger, and true believers; they connect them to 3:68, 33:6, 8:72, and 9:71.
TABATABAI:5:55-56/r1.anchor: جماعة من مفسري القوم إشتراكهما مع ما قبلهما وما بعدهما

TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects a unified context: although the surah was revealed late, its verses came down at different times, as their content and occasions of revelation show; adjacency does not prove common occasion or context.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r2.anchor: فليس مجرد وقوع الآية بعد الآية أو قبل الآية يدل على وحدة السياق

TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r5.claim: The alternative reading of bowing makes the verse say that believers' guardians are God, the Messenger, and faithful worshippers who submit to God's lordship in obedience, or give alms while poor.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r5.anchor: ويعود معنى الآية إلى أنه ليس أولياؤكم اليهود والنصارى والمنافقين بل أولياؤكم الله ورسوله

TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r1.claim: It is improper to call the Prophet a supporter of believers in the relevant religious sense; support is rendered to God's religion, which God legislates and the Messenger and believers uphold.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r1.anchor: على أنه ليس من الجائز أن يعد النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وليا للمؤمنين بمعنى ولاية النصرة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r4.claim: Since believers are bound to God's religious law, the Qur'an describes God as supporting those who support Him and as supporting His messengers and believers.

TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r5.claim: Religion cannot belong only to believers with the Prophet outside it and then make him their supporter: he shares every religious distinction in its fullest measure, and the Qur'an never calls him their supporter.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r5.anchor: ولا في آية واحدة، وحاشا ساحة الكلام الإلهي أن يساهل

TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r2.claim: The promise of victory fits authority, love, and support alike; religious victory comes through connection to God and His Messenger by any means.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r2.anchor: فإن الغلبة كما تناسب الولاية بمعنى النصرة، كذلك تناسب ولاية التصرف وكذا ولاية المحبة والمودة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r3.claim: Numerous Shia and Sunni reports say both verses were revealed about Ali when he gave his ring during prayer.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r3.anchor: على أن الروايات متكاثرة من طرق الشيعة وأهل السنة على أن الآيتين نازلتان في أمير المؤمنين علي عليه السلام لما تصدق بخاتمه وهو في الصلاة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r4.claim: Rejecting abundant transmitted occasions of revelation would make transmitted occasions for any Qur’anic verse unreliable.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r4.anchor: لم يصح الركون إلى شيء من أسباب النزول المأثورة في شيء من آيات القرآن

TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r2.claim: Close reading rejects all objections: these verses do not serve the prior context’s support theme, even if earlier verses did.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r2.anchor: لكن التدبر في الآية وما يناظرها من الآيات يوجب سقوط الوجوه المذكورة جميعا

TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r5.claim: The coordinated list under one singular wali indicates one sense of wilāya for God, the Messenger, and believers; the next verse likewise treats them together as God’s party.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r5.anchor: على ما يدل على وحدة ما في معنى الولاية المذكورة فيه

TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r7.claim: Tawallā means taking as a wali; the definite believers refer back to the believers described in the preceding verse.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r7.anchor: التولي هو الأخذ وليا، و { الذين آمنوا } مفيد للعهد والمراد به المذكور في الآية السابقة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r8.claim: The stated result clause substitutes for a major premise: whoever takes them as wali prevails because he joins God’s party, indirectly identifying them as that party.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r8.anchor: واقع موقع الجزاء وليس به بل هو من قبيل وضع الكبرى موضع النتيجة للدلالة على علة الحكم

TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r9.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r9.claim: Al-Rāghib defines a ḥizb as a group marked by strength or toughness.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r9.anchor: والحزب على ما ذكره الراغب جماعة فيها غلظ

TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r1.claim: Qur’an describes God’s party as believers who do not love those opposing God and His Messenger, even if close relatives; they are strengthened by the Spirit and called successful.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r1.anchor: أولئك حزب الله ألا إن حزب الله هم المفلحون

TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r2.claim: Falāḥ means attaining one’s aim, including victory and gaining control over what one seeks.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r2.anchor: والفلاح الظفر وإدراك البغية التي هي الغلبة والاستيلاء على المراد

TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r3.claim: Unqualified victory and success mean ultimate happiness and truth, overcoming misery and falsehood in both worlds: a righteous earthly life and nearness to the Lord hereafter.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r3.anchor: فالمراد الغلبة المطلقة والفلاح المطلق أي الظفر بالسعادة والفوز بالحق والغلبة على الشقاء، وإدحاض الباطل في الدنيا والآخرة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#12/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:5:55-56#12/r1.claim: In the report’s continuation, the Prophet asks the petitioner who gave him the ring; after he says Ali gave it while bowing, the Prophet declares Ali his successor in wilāya, those present assent, and 5:56 is revealed.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#12/r1.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم علي وليكم بعدي قالوا رضينا بالله ربا، وبمحمد نبيا

TABATABAI:5:55-56#17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#17/r2.speaker: ابن سلام
TABATABAI:5:55-56#17/r2.claim: Ibn Salam reports that converts ostracized by their people witnessed Ali give his ring while bowing; the Prophet recited both verses after learning of the gift.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#17/r2.anchor: من صحيح النسائي عن ابن سلام قال أتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلنا إن قومنا حادونا لما صدقنا الله ورسوله

TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r1.claim: In Ibn Abbas's report, the petitioner identifies Ali as the ring-giver and says he gave it while bowing; the Prophet then recites 5:56, completing the response to Ibn Salam's group's complaint.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r1.anchor: خرج إلى المسجد والناس بين قائم وراكع، وبصر بسائل

TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r4.claim: The author says reports of the ring-giving occasion are numerous and available in their cited books; he selected several accounts because their wording of the episode varies.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r4.anchor: أقول والروايات في نزول الآيتين في قصة التصدق بالخاتم كثيرة أخرجنا عدة منها من كتاب غاية المرام للبحراني

TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r5.claim: The author says Companions and Imams widely transmitted the episode, and major tafsir and hadith authorities including Ahmad, al-Nasa'i, al-Tabari, and al-Tabarani accepted it without refutation; theologians also acknowledged its report.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r5.anchor: وقد اتفق على نقلها من غير رد أئمة التفسير المأثور كأحمد والنسائي والطبري والطبراني وعبد بن حميد

TABRISI:5:55-56/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56/r9.claim: Ḥizb means a party or group; it derives from something that befalls a person and refers to people with similar hearts and deeds or those who gather together.
TABRISI:5:55-56/r9.anchor: والحزب الطائفة والجماعة وأصله من قولهم

TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r3.claim: Man is the subject; yatawalla has a jussive pronoun returning to it, and the fa clause is jussive by its conditional force; the conditional phrase is the subject's predicate.
TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r3.anchor: وموضع من رفع بالابتداء وفي يتول ضمير يعود إلى من

TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r2.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r2.claim: Ḥassān ibn Thābit's poem praises Abū Ḥasan for giving zakāt while bowing and says God revealed and established the best form of allegiance for him.
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r2.anchor: فأنت الذي أعطيت إذ كنت راكعا زكاة فدتك النفس

TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r11.claim: Taking Allah as patron is obeying Him, the Messenger is following his command, and the believers means allegiance and support.
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r11.anchor: ومن يتول الله } بالقيام بطاعته { ورسوله } باتباع أمره { والذين آمنوا } بالموالاة والنصرة

TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r12.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r12.claim: Al-Hasan glosses ḥizb Allāh as God’s soldiers, who prevail over their enemies.
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r12.anchor: فإن حزب الله } أي جند الله عن الحسن

TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r13.claim: Another gloss takes ḥizb Allāh to mean God’s helpers.
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r13.anchor: وقيل أنصار الله { هم الغالبون } الظاهرون على أعدائهم الظافرون بهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437/r1.claim: To take God, His Messenger, and the believers as guardians means to undertake obedience to God and support His Messenger and the believers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437/r1.anchor: معناه: من يتول القيام بطاعة الله ونصرة رسوله والمؤمنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies those who take these guardians as the Emigrants, the Helpers, and later believers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: "يريد المهاجرين والأنصار والذين آمنوا من بعدهم"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r1.claim: The clause is the predicate of the conditional's subject, with its meaning supplying the return to the initial subject; it answers the condition, so it begins with fa.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r1.anchor: جملة واقعة موقع خبر المبتدأ، والعائد إلى الابتداء معناها, لأن المعنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r2.claim: In Arabic, a hizb is a person's companions who share his position; believers are God's party and unbelievers Satan's party.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r2.anchor: ومعنى الحزب في اللغة: أصحاب الرجل الذين معه على رأيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r3.claim: Al-Farra glosses hizb as a class or kind of people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء: الحزب: الصنف من الناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r4.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi says hizb means a group.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan glosses God's party as God's army.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r6.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r6.claim: Another exegete glosses God's party as God's supporters.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r7.speaker: أبو روق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r7.claim: Abu Rawq glosses God's party as God's friends.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r8.speaker: أبو العالية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r8.claim: Abu al-Aliya glosses God's party as His adherents.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r9.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r9.claim: Al-Akhfash defines God's party as those who follow His religion and obey Him, whom He then supports.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r9.anchor: وقال الأخفش: حزب الله الذين يدينون بدينه ويطيعونه فينصرهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r10.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r10.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets victory as killing the Jews and expelling them from their homes, while Abd Allah ibn Salam and his companions who allied with God and His Messenger remained.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p437#2/r10.anchor: وقال الكلبي في قوله: {هم الغالبون} "فقتلوا اليهود وأجلوهم من ديارهم

QASHANI:5:55-56/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:55-56/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:55-56/r6.claim: Whoever allies with God, the Messenger, and believers belongs to God's people.

QASHANI:5:55-56/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:55-56/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:55-56/r7.claim: God's people are victorious through God.
QASHANI:5:55-56/r7.anchor: فهو من أهل الله، وإن أهل الله { هم الغالبون } بالله.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r4.claim: Taking God, the Messenger, and believers as patrons means undertaking obedience to God and supporting His Messenger and believers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r4.anchor: { ومن يتول الله ورسوله } يتولى القيام بطاعته ونصرة رسوله والمؤمنين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r5.claim: God's party means His troops and supporters of His religion; they overcame the Jews and expelled them from their homes.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r5.anchor: { فإن حزب الله } جند الله وأنصار دينه { هم الغالبون } غلبوا اليهود فأجلوهم من ديارهم،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r6.claim: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his companions remained loyal to God and His Messenger.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r6.anchor: وبقي عبد الله بن سلام وأصحابه الذين تولوا الله ورسوله.

ELMALILI:5:56-57/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:56-57/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:56-57/r1.claim: Lexically, a ḥizb is a person’s companions who follow his opinion, gathered together for a pressing matter.
ELMALILI:5:56-57/r1.anchor: “Hizb” lügatta bir zâtın re’yine tâbi‘olup kendisiyle beraber bulunan ashâbıdır ki kendilerini tazyik eden bir iş için toplanmış kimseler demektir.

ELMALILI:5:56-57/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:56-57/r2.speaker: المفسرون
ELMALILI:5:56-57/r2.claim: Exegetes gloss God’s party as God’s army, friends, helpers, or partisans.
ELMALILI:5:56-57/r2.anchor: حِزْبَ ٱللَّهِ unvânını müfessirîn جُنْدُ االله، أَوْلِيَاءُ االله، أَنْصَارُ االله، شِيـْعَةُ االله diye muhtelif tâbirlerle tefsir etmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:5:56-57/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:56-57/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:56-57/r3.claim: Only God’s party truly triumphs; other victories are outward or temporary because ultimate guardianship belongs to God.
ELMALILI:5:56-57/r3.anchor: Asıl velâyet Allah’ındır. Diğerlerinin galebesi sûrî veya muvakkattir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:56/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:56/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:56/r1.claim: Whoever takes Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as allies belongs to God’s party, which will surely prevail.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:56/r1.anchor: Kim Allah’ı, peygamberini ve iman edenleri velî edinirse bilsin ki Allah’tan yana olanlar mutlaka galip geleceklerdir.

SULAMI:v1p180#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r1.claim: Sahl says repentance has stations and states, and true repentance is the alliance with God and His Messenger described in this verse.
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r1.anchor: قال سهل : التوبة لها مقامات وحالات

SULAMI:v1p180#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r2.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r2.claim: Al-Qasim says alliance with God proceeds through alliance with His Messenger, which proceeds through alliance with exemplary elders among God's servants; honoring them is required for progress in divine alliance.
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r2.anchor: قال القاسم : موالاة الله مشتقة من موالاة رسوله وموالاة الرسول مشتقة من موالاة السادة

SULAMI:v1p180#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r3.speaker: النبي
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r3.claim: The Prophet says that honoring an aged Muslim is part of honoring God's majesty.
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r3.anchor: فإن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ' من تعظيم جلال الله إكرام ذي الشيبة المسلم ' ،

SULAMI:v1p180#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r4.speaker: النبي
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r4.claim: The Prophet says revering elders is part of reverence for God.
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r4.anchor: وقال : صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' بجلوا المشايخ فإن تبجيل المشايخ من إجلال الله '

SULAMI:v1p180#4/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r5.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r5.claim: Sahl says God's party overcomes its own lower desires, wishes, and aims.
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r5.anchor: وقال سهل في قوله : ﴿ فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون ﴾ قال : لأهوائهم وإراداتهم

SULAMI:v1p180#4/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r6.claim: Others define God's party as His elect, steadfast with Him under the conditions of uprightness.
SULAMI:v1p180#4/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم : حزب الله أهل خاصته والقائمون معه على شرائط الاستقامة

TUSTARI:5:56/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:5:56/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:5:56/r1.claim: God's party are victorious over the desires of their own souls.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that Abdullah ibn Salam and fellow converts complained of Jewish rejection; in the mosque, a beggar identified Ali as the person who gave him a gold ring while bowing, and Muhammad recited the verse ending at 5:56.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أقبل عبد الله بن سلام ومعه نفر من قومه قد آمنوا، فقالوا: يا رسول الله إن منازلنا بعيدة وليس لنا مجلس ولا متحدث،

SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r1.claim: Man is a conditional noun in the nominative as the sentence’s subject.
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r1.anchor: من شرط في محل رفع بالابتداء

SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r2.claim: One analysis makes “God’s party are the triumphant” the conditional answer, supporting grammarians who do not require a resumptive pronoun for a conditional subject.
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r2.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون جوابا للشرط، وبه يحتج من لا يشترط عود ضمير

SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r3.claim: An objection is that God’s party repeats the meaning of the conditional subject; al-Akhfash permits such repetition, with an understood pronoun and divine affiliation honoring the party.
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r3.anchor: إنما جاز ذلك لأن المراد بحزب الله هو نفس المبتدأ

SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r4.claim: Alternatively, the answer is omitted and understood as becoming part of God’s triumphant party or being helped; the following clause indicates it.
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الجواب محذوفا لدلالة الكلام عليه أي: ومن يتول الله ورسوله

SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r5.claim: The clause is in the jussive position if it is the conditional answer; it has no syntactic position if it merely indicates an omitted answer.
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r5.anchor: في محل جزم إن جعلناه جوابا للشرط، ولا محل له إن جعلناه دالا على الجواب

SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r6.claim: “They” can be a pronoun of separation, or a new subject whose predicate is “the triumphant”; that sentence then predicates the إن clause.
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r6.anchor: وقوله: " هم " يحتمل أن يكون فصلا وأن يكون مبتدأ و " الغالبون " خبره

SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r7.claim: Ḥizb means a distinct group marked by force and severity.
SAMIN-DURR:5:56/r7.anchor: والحزب: الجماعة فيها غلظة وشدة، فهو جماعة خاصة

NASHR:v1p439/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p439/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p439/r1.claim: For medial hamza separated after a long vowel, Iraqi transmitters ease it as they ease connected medial hamza: replace open hamza with waw after damma or ya after kasra, or pronounce it between; the remaining seven sūras use between-between.
NASHR:v1p439/r1.anchor: فسهل أيضا هذا القسم من سهل الهمز المتوسط المنفصل الواقع بعد حروف المد من العراقيين

NASHR:v1p439/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p439/r2.speaker: يونس والكسائي
NASHR:v1p439/r2.claim: Yunus and al-Kisāʾī report Arab substitution and assimilation of hamza after original waw or ya; Sibawayh also transmits it but confines it to attested usage rather than a productive rule.
NASHR:v1p439/r2.anchor: حكى سماع ذلك من العرب يونس والكسائي، وحكاه أيضا سيبويه، ولكنه لم يقسه

NASHR:v1p439/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p439/r3.speaker: حمزة
NASHR:v1p439/r3.claim: A group of readers accepts substituting and assimilating hamza after original waw or ya; the source explicitly transmits this reading from Hamza.
NASHR:v1p439/r3.anchor: ووافق على الإبدال والإدغام في ذلك جماعة من القراء، وجاء أيضا منصوصا عن حمزة

NASHR:v1p439/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p439/r4.speaker: ابن بليمة
NASHR:v1p439/r4.claim: Ibn Bulayma limits substitution and assimilation to شيء، هيئة، and موئلا rather than applying it productively.
NASHR:v1p439/r4.anchor: وخصه أبو علي بن بليمة (بشيء، وهيئة، وموئلا) فقط، فلم يجعله مطردا

NASHR:v1p439/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p439/r5.speaker: ابن مجاهد
NASHR:v1p439/r5.claim: Ibn Mujahid and the majority prefer transmission alone as the rule, preserving the productive analogy of retaining original waw and ya rather than assimilating them.
NASHR:v1p439/r5.anchor: والجمهور، وهو اختيار ابن مجاهد وغيره، وهو القياس المطرد إجماعا

NASHR:v1p439/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p439/r6.speaker: أبو العلاء
NASHR:v1p439/r6.claim: Abu al-ʿAlāʾ permits assimilation after a weak-letter glide but not after a long vowel, reasoning that a long vowel cannot be assimilated.
NASHR:v1p439/r6.anchor: انفرد الحافظ أبو العلاء فخص جواز الإدغام من ذلك بحرف اللين ولم يجزه بحرف المد

NASHR:v1p439/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p439/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p439/r7.claim: The author rejects Abu al-ʿAlāʾ's restriction: when a long vowel is augmentative assimilation is required; the assimilation is estimated, as in Abu ʿAmr's examples نودي يا موسى and هو والذين آمنوا.
NASHR:v1p439/r7.anchor: (والجواب) عن ذلك أن الإدغام فيه تقديري، فإنا لما لفظنا بياء مشددة وواو مشددة

IBNHISHAM:v2p49#2/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p49#2/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v2p49#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq connects 5:55–56 to Ubadah's allegiance to God, His Messenger, and the believers, and his disavowal of Banu Qaynuqa and their pact.
IBNHISHAM:v2p49#2/r3.anchor: وذكر لتولي عبادة بن الصامت الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا، وتبرئه من بني قينقاع وحلفهم وولايتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v6p171#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171#2/r1.claim: To ally oneself with God, the Messenger, and believers is the meaning of taking them as awliya.

ALUSI-FULL:v6p171#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171#2/r2.claim: The explicit phrase ‘those who believe’ replaces a pronoun to preserve the earlier point that God is primary in guardianship.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171#2/r2.anchor: وأوثر الإظهار على الإضمار رعاية لمامر من نكتة بيان أصالته تعالى فى الولاية

ALUSI-FULL:v6p171#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171#2/r3.claim: Hizb means a party or group generally, or specifically a group marked by strength; it is attached especially to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171#2/r3.anchor: حيث أضيف الحزب أى الطائفة والجماعة مطلقا أو الجماعة التى فيها شدة إليه تعالى خاصة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p171#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171#2/r4.claim: The apparent noun ‘God’s party’ can stand for the pronoun referring to those who ally, honoring them and proving their victory; many grammarians take the clause as the answer’s evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171#2/r4.anchor: فانهم حزب الله تعالى هم الغالبون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r1.claim: To take God, His Messenger, and believers as allies means undertaking obedience to God and supporting His Messenger and the believers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r1.anchor: {ومن يتول الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا} يعني: يتولى القيام بطاعة الله ونصرة رسوله والمؤمنين،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the believers here as the Emigrants and the Helpers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: يريد المهاجرين والأنصار،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r3.claim: God’s party means the supporters of God’s religion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r3.anchor: {فإن حزب الله} يعني: أنصار دين الله،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r4.claim: Those who belong to God’s party are the ones who prevail.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p73/r4.anchor: {فإن حزب الله} يعني: أنصار دين الله، {هم الغالبون}

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:56-57/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:56-57/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:56-57/r1.claim: Taking God, the Messenger, and believers as allies is the sense of taking them as patrons.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:56-57/r1.anchor: ومن يتخذهم أولياء. { فإن حزب الله هم

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:56-57/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:56-57/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:56-57/r2.claim: The explicit “God’s party” replaces a pronoun to spell out the proof, honor the group, and imply that allies of others belong to Satan’s party.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:56-57/r2.anchor: فهم حزب الله وحزب الله هم الغالبون

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:56-57/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:56-57/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:56-57/r3.claim: A ḥizb is a group assembled for a matter that has confronted or occupied them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:56-57/r3.anchor: وأصل الحزب القوم يجتمعون لأمر حز بهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r1.claim: The preceding implication is that those allying with others join Satan’s party and lose; this verse states the converse, allegiance to God, His Messenger, and believers.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r2.claim: To ally with God is to strive to be allied to the One who possesses all sources of might.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r2.anchor: يجتهد في ولاية الذي له مجامع العز

BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r3.claim: The allies are named again for blessing and to state the intended referents explicitly; the Messenger is described as one formed by the Qur’an.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r3.anchor: وأعاد ذكر من خص الولاية بهم تبركا بأسمائهم وتصريحا بالمقصود

BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r4.claim: Instead of leaving the understood predicate ‘they are victorious,’ the verse names God’s party to honor and encourage them to choose His allegiance.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r4.anchor: ولكنه أظهر ما شرفهم به ترغيبا لهم في ولايته

BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r5.claim: God’s party is the group gathered around what pleases the Supreme King, including what has been made hard for them; they alone prevail, while opponents are defeated and gathered for Hell.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p484/r5.anchor: القوم الذين يجمعهم على ما يرضي الملك الأعلى ما حزبهم أي اشتد عليهم فيه

DURR-FULL:v3p106/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r1.claim: In the ring-giving report, the noon caller’s question established that the beggar received it from Ali while he was bowing; the Prophet then recited the promise of victory for God’s party.
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r1.anchor: وخرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: أعطاك أحد شيئا قال: نعم

DURR-FULL:v3p106#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p106#2/r2.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p106#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says God identifies the winners to reassure believers not to fear a reversal of fortune or calamity.
DURR-FULL:v3p106#2/r2.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {ومن يتول الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون}

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1163/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1163/r1.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1163/r1.claim: ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit says the verse came down after he declared allegiance to God and His Messenger and disavowed his alliance with Banū Qaynuqāʿ.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1163/r1.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت قال : نزلت : ومن يتول الله ورسوله والذين امنوا فان حزب الله هم الغالبون وذاك لقول عبادة بن الصامت

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1163/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1163/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1163/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says God tells them who will prevail, so they should not fear loss of power or a reversal of fortune.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1163/r2.anchor: عن السدى قوله : فان حزب الله هم الغالبون قال : ثم اخبرهم ، يعني الرب عز وجل من الغالب فقال : لا تخافوا الدولة ولا الدائرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240#2/r1.claim: The clause gives the reason for the implied conditional result: they prevail because they belong to God's party.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240#2/r1.anchor: فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون } دليل على جواب الشرط بذكر علة الجواب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p384/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p384/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p384/r1.claim: Al-Hasan explains God's party as God's troops.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p384/r1.anchor: فأما حزب الله فقال الحسن هم جند الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p384/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p384/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p384/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda explains God's party as God's helpers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p384/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة أنصار الله ثم فيه قولان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p384/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p384/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p384/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies God's party as the Emigrants and the Helpers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p384/r3.anchor: أحدهما أنهم المهاجرون والأنصار قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p384/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p384/r4.speaker: أبو سليمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p384/r4.claim: Abu Sulayman identifies God's party as the Helpers.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says the preceding verses were revealed about ʿUbada ibn al-Samit, who renounced his Jewish alliance and accepted the guardianship of God, the Messenger, and the believers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r1.anchor: أن هذه الآيات كلها نزلت في عبادة بن الصامت، رضي الله عنه، حين تبرأ من حلف يهود،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir links God’s party prevailing to 58:21–22, where God decrees victory for His messengers and describes the successful party of God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r2.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {كتب الله لأغلبن أنا ورسلي إن الله قوي عزيز. لا تجد قوما يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r3.claim: Whoever accepts God’s, His Messenger’s, and the believers’ guardianship succeeds in this world and the next, and is victorious in both.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r3.anchor: فكل من رضي بولاية (3) الله ورسوله والمؤمنين فهو مفلح في الدنيا والآخرة [ومنصور في الدنيا والآخرة]

JISHUMI:v3p2002/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r1.claim: A hizb is a party or group; its root sense is an affliction that befalls someone, and people with common hearts and deeds form a party even without meeting.
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r1.anchor: الحزب: الطائفة، والجماعة، والأحزاب الجمع، وأصله النائبة، من قولهم: حزبه الأمر

JISHUMI:v3p2002/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r2.claim: The description of parties echoes the verse that communities split into factions, each rejoicing in what it has.
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r2.anchor: فتقطعوا أمرهم بينهم زبرا كل حزب بما لديهم فرحون (53)

JISHUMI:v3p2002/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r4.claim: من is the subject and the following clause its predicate, with an implied result: whoever allies with God is victorious.
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r4.anchor: (من) في قوله: ومن يتول الله ورسوله مبتدأ، والجملة بعده خبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r1.claim: The explicit phrase حزب الله replaces a pronoun; the meaning is that they are the ones who prevail.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r1.anchor: من إقامة الظاهر مقام المضمر ومعناه فإنهم هم الغالبون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r2.claim: Naming them God’s party marks their defining affiliation; ḥizb originally means a group assembled around its cause.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r2.anchor: ولكنهم بذلك جعلوا اعلاما لكونهم حزب الله وأصل الحزب القوم يجتمعون لأمر حزبهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r3.claim: He also allows حزب الله to refer specifically to the Messenger and the believers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد بحزب الله الرسول والمؤمنين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r4.claim: Whoever takes them as patrons has thereby taken God’s party as patron and gained support from one none can overcome.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p683/r4.anchor: ومن يتولهم فقد تولى حزب الله واعتضد بمن لا يغالب

MUQATIL:5:55-57/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:55-57/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:55-57/r2.claim: In this continuation, those believers whom one allies with refer to ʿAli b. Abi Talib.
MUQATIL:5:55-57/r2.anchor: { ومن يتول الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا } ، يعنى على بن أبى طالب

MUQATIL:5:55-57/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:55-57/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:55-57/r3.claim: God's party means the adherents of God, His Messenger, and the believers, who are victorious; the reference begins with ʿAli and then includes Muslims and believing People of the Book such as ʿAbd Allah b. Salam.
MUQATIL:5:55-57/r3.anchor: يعنى شيعة الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا هم الغالبون، فبدأ بعلى بن أبى طالب، رضى الله عنه، قبل المسلمين

MUQATIL:5:55-57/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:55-57/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:55-57/r4.claim: The believers prevailed over the Jews by killing and expelling them from Medina to Syria, Adhriʿat, and Jericho.
MUQATIL:5:55-57/r4.anchor: فيهم عبدالله بن سلام وغيره هم الغالبون لليهود، حين قتلوهم وأجلوهم من المدينة إلى الشام وأذرعات وأريحا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p289/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p289/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p289/r1.claim: To take God, the Messenger, and believers as allies may mean making them protectors or becoming their ally.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p289/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p289/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p289/r2.claim: «God’s party» may replace a pronoun, meaning «they are the victors».
NASAFI-FULL:v1p289/r2.anchor: من إقامة الظاهر مقام الضمير أى فإنهم هم الغالبون

NASAFI-FULL:v1p289/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p289/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p289/r3.claim: Alternatively, God’s party means the Messenger and believers; whoever allies with them joins a force that cannot be overcome.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p289/r3.anchor: أو المراد بحزب الله الرسول والمؤمنون

NASAFI-FULL:v1p289/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p289/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p289/r4.claim: A ḥizb is a group gathered around a matter; its root also describes a matter striking or affecting people.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p289/r4.anchor: وأصل الحزب القوم يجتمعون الأمر حزبهم أى أصابهم

BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r11.claim: Whoever takes God, the Messenger, and believers as allies will be victorious.
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r11.anchor: {ومن يتول الله ورسوله والذين ءامنوا} أي ومن يتخذهم أولياء {فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون}

BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r12.claim: The explicit phrase God's party replaces a pronoun to prove the outcome: those who ally with these figures are God's party and therefore victorious; it honors them and implies other allies belong to Satan's party.
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r12.anchor: ولكن وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر تنبيها على البرهان عليه وكأنه قيل ومن يتول هؤلاء فهم حزب الله وحزب الله هم الغالبون

BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r13.claim: Hizb means a person's companions or supporters, and also a group gathered for a shared cause.
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r13.anchor: وحزب الرجل أصحابه والحزب الطائفة يجتمعون لأمر حزبهم أي أصابهم

QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r1.claim: Whoever entrusts his affairs to God, obeys His Messenger, and allies with Muslims belongs to God's party.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r1.anchor: أي من فوض أمره إلى الله، وامتثل أمر رسوله، ووالى المسلمين، فهو من حزب الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r2.claim: Alternatively, taking God and believers as allies means undertaking obedience to God and supporting the Messenger and believers.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r2.anchor: وقيل: أي ومن يتولى القيام بطاعة الله ونصرة رسوله والمؤمنين.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r3.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r3.claim: Al-Hasan explains God's party as God's army.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r3.anchor: قال الحسن: حزب الله جند الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r4.claim: Another view glosses God's party as supporters; the cited poem uses hizbi to mean 'my supporter.'
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r4.anchor: وقال غيره: أنصار الله قال الشاعر: وكيف أضوى وبلال حزبي أي ناصري.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r5.claim: The believers are God's party and overcame the Jews through captivity, killing, expulsion, and jizya.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r5.anchor: والمؤمنون حزب الله فلا جرم غلبوا اليهود بالسبي والقتل والإجلاء وضرب الجزية.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r6.claim: Hizb means a class of people and derives from an incident befalling someone; it can also mean a man's companions.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r6.anchor: والحزب الصنف من الناس وأصله من النائبة من قولهم: حزبه كذا أي نابه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r7.claim: Hizb can mean a nightly recitation portion, as in the hadith about missing one's nightly hizb; it also means a Qur'an portion or faction, and tahazzub means gathering.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r8.claim: Al-ahzab are factions gathered to fight prophets; 'hisbahu amr' means an affair afflicted him.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:56/r8.anchor: والأحزاب: الطوائف التي تجتمع على محاربة الأنبياء. وحزبه أمر أي أصابه.
